lessons.lesson: Anchor stop prices to the expected fill, not the last reference close, whenever a name has gapped or is reacting to news. Check that the stated stop distance (e.g. 10%) still holds at the likely entry price before approving.
evidence: 2026-10-20 DPZ: stop of $274.88 was set 10% under the $305.42 reference close, but the buy filled at $316.58 (about 3.7% higher), so the stop sat about 13% below entry instead of the intended 10%.
2026-10-20 MSCI rejected partly because its stop was anchored to the pre-earnings close (same flaw; not yet graded, pending).

2026-10-23 VRSN: filled at $292.23, 4.7% below the $306.48 menu close after the 10-22 print (a gap down). The PM anchored the stop to the fill per this lesson; a menu-close stop would have sat about 14% below the fill. Applied correctly, not a graded call (pending).
2026-10-26 VRSN: the PM anchored the stop (278) to the expected fill near $303, which filled at $303.08, so the stop sits about 8.3% under the fill as intended. Applied correctly, not graded.

2026-10-26 DPZ: the held position's invalidation ($274.88) is still anchored to the pre-fill reference close and sits about 13% below the $316.58 fill; the PM review flags it as unfixed. Re-anchor existing theses to the actual fill when reviewing held positions.

2026-10-27 MSM: the PM wrote the invalidation against the actual fill (filled at the $118.72 menu close, so the ~9% distance held). DPZ's $274.88 invalidation is still not re-anchored (PM and Fundamentals reviews both flag it); DPZ is -1.4% on the fill.
